label: LALA
phenotype: Reduced binding to FcgammaRI, FcgammaRIIa and FcgammaRIIIa and reduced C1q binding; ADCC, ADCP and CDC reduced but not abolished.
notes: The most widely used silencing pair and the most widely over-trusted. Residual FcgammaR binding is repeatedly documented; LALA is attenuating, not null. Derived from the murine OKT3 lower-hinge alanine substitutions.

label: LALA-PG
phenotype: Eliminates measurable FcgammaRI, FcgammaRII and FcgammaRIII binding and abolishes C1q binding and complement fixation; ADCC and ADCP not detected.
notes: P329G removes the proline-sandwich contact with the receptor FG loop, so the two mechanisms are additive rather than redundant. Transfers to murine IgG2a, which makes it useful for matched surrogate work.

label: LALA-PS
phenotype: Reduced FcgammaR binding and reduced C1q binding.
notes: P331S contributes mainly on the complement arm.

label: LALAGA
phenotype: Reduced FcgammaR binding and reduced C1q binding.
notes: G237A extends the lower-hinge alanine patch.

label: LALA-LR
phenotype: Reduced FcgammaR binding and reduced C1q binding.

label: LALA-DS
phenotype: Reduced FcgammaR binding and reduced C1q binding.

label: LE
phenotype: Decreased binding to cell-surface FcgammaR; ADCC reduced.
notes: Single-substitution silencing; weaker and less complete than paired variants.

label: FE
phenotype: Reduced FcgammaR binding and reduced C1q binding.

label: TM
phenotype: Decreased binding to FcgammaRI, FcgammaRII, FcgammaRIII and C1q; CDC reduced.
notes: Often called the "triple mutant". Reported in the literature both as L234F/L235E/P331S and, in older text, as P331S/L234E/L235F; the residue identities at 234 and 235 are transposed between those two renderings.

label: FQQ
phenotype: Reduced FcgammaR binding and reduced C1q binding.
notes: K322Q targets the complement arm specifically.

label: FQQ-YTE
phenotype: Reduced FcgammaR and C1q binding with extended half-life via enhanced FcRn binding at pH 6.0.
notes: A deliberate combination of a silencing module and a half-life module. Useful as the worked example of modular Fc engineering, and of its developability cost.

label: GRLR
phenotype: Decreased binding to all FcgammaR; ADCC reduced.
notes: Arginine substitutions introduce steric and electrostatic disruption at the interface.

label: STR
phenotype: No detectable FcgammaR binding; ADCC and CDC undetectable; C1q binding abrogated.
notes: Designed explicitly to reach completeness rather than attenuation, with the G236R substitution doing much of the work.

label: N297A
phenotype: Removes the conserved CH2 N-glycan; decreased FcgammaRI and FcgammaRIIIa binding and decreased C1q binding.
notes: Silences by deleting the glycan rather than by editing the protein interface, and therefore also destabilizes CH2 and lowers the thermal transition. Residual binding is documented.

label: N297G
phenotype: Glycan knockout; ADCC reduced and FcgammaR binding reduced.
notes: Glycine gives more backbone flexibility than alanine at the same position.

label: N297Q
phenotype: Glycan knockout; ADCC reduced and FcgammaR binding reduced.

label: DA
phenotype: Decreased binding to FcgammaRI, FcgammaRII and FcgammaRIII; ADCC and ADCP reduced.
notes: D265 is a direct interface contact in every Fc-FcgammaR complex in this atlas.

label: DAPA
phenotype: Combines interface disruption with glycan removal; FcgammaR binding and effector function strongly reduced.
notes: Two mechanistically distinct silencing routes stacked on one molecule.

label: PG
phenotype: Reduced FcgammaR binding and reduced C1q binding.
notes: Destroys the proline sandwich formed with the receptor FG loop tryptophans.

label: L328R
phenotype: Reduced FcgammaR binding and reduced C1q binding.

label: E233P
phenotype: Prevents FcgammaRI binding; decreased binding to FcgammaRI, II and III.
notes: One of the earliest rationally designed lower-hinge silencing substitutions.

label: IgG2-like lower hinge
phenotype: Decreased FcgammaR binding by converting the IgG1 lower hinge to an IgG2-like motif.
notes: Includes a residue deletion, so this variant cannot be represented as a pure substitution set and is flagged as non-substitutional.

label: IgG1 sigma
phenotype: Near-complete elimination of FcgammaRI, FcgammaRIIa, FcgammaRIIb and FcgammaRIIIa binding; ADCC and CDC abolished; FcRn binding retained.
notes: The IgG1 counterpart of IgG2-sigma, built by importing the sigma residue set onto an IgG1 frame.

label: IgG2 sigma
phenotype: Near-complete elimination of FcgammaRI, FcgammaRIIa, FcgammaRIIb and FcgammaRIIIa binding; undetectable ADCC, ADCP and CDC; FcRn binding retained.
notes: NUMBERING DISPUTE. The primary publication and most reviews write the first substitution as V234A. IMGT lists the same variant as V235A (G2v3). This is a real consequence of the shorter IgG2 lower hinge: the IgG1 and IgG2 hinges cannot be aligned without a gap, so the EU index assigned to the valine depends on where that gap is placed. Under this package's alignment EU 234 in IgG2 is a gap and the valine sits at EU 235, which reproduces the IMGT assignment from sequence alone. The substitution is therefore held in `disputed_mutations` rather than asserted at one index. Both renderings mean the same physical valine. See docs/numbering.md.

label: IgG2m4
phenotype: Reduced binding to all FcgammaR and reduced C1q binding; ADCC, ADCP and CDC reduced.
notes: A cross-subclass design that imports four IgG4 residues onto an IgG2 frame.

label: IgG4 PAA
phenotype: Decreased binding to FcgammaRI, FcgammaRIIa and FcgammaRIIIa; ADCC and CDC reduced; S228P prevents Fab-arm exchange.
notes: Bundles a silencing module with a stability module. The S228P hinge fix addresses half-molecule exchange, not effector function.

label: FALA
phenotype: Reduced FcgammaR binding and reduced C1q binding.
notes: The IgG4 positional equivalent of LALA; position 234 is phenylalanine in IgG4.

label: SPLE
phenotype: Decreased FcgammaRI binding with half-life unchanged; S228P prevents Fab-arm exchange.

label: LEPG
phenotype: Reduced FcgammaR binding and reduced C1q binding.

label: IgG2/IgG4 hybrid
phenotype: Reduced FcgammaR binding and reduced C1q binding.
notes: A chimeric constant region rather than a point-variant series, and one of the few silencing designs with a named approved therapeutic attached. Contains a deletion and is flagged as non-substitutional. The parent frame is recorded as IgG4 because the wild-type residues implied by the substitution set (E233, F234, L235, G236) are the IgG4 residues; the changes convert an IgG4 lower hinge toward the IgG2 motif. Curating this record against IgG2, as its IMGT G2G4v1 label invites, fails sequence validation at all four positions.

label: DE
phenotype: Increased FcgammaRIIIa binding; ADCC enhanced; ADCP with FcgammaRII increased modestly.
notes: The parent of the aspartate/glutamate charge-engineering series.

label: DLE
phenotype: Increased FcgammaRIIIa binding and decreased FcgammaRIIb binding; ADCC enhanced; CDC eliminated.
notes: A useful counterexample to the assumption that enhancement is monotonic. A330L raises ADCC while ablating complement, so the same variant is an enhancing and a silencing design depending on the axis measured.

label: GASDALIE
phenotype: Increased FcgammaRIIIa and FcgammaRIIa binding; ADCC and ADCP enhanced; FcgammaRI-mediated phagocytosis increased 1.87-fold; CDC absent.
notes: Widely used in preclinical immuno-oncology models.

label: GASDIE
phenotype: Increased FcgammaRIIIa binding and FcgammaRIIa binding above 70-fold with a 15-fold shift in the FcgammaRIIa/FcgammaRIIb ratio; ADCC and ADCP enhanced; CDC little changed.

label: GAALIE
phenotype: Increased FcgammaRIIIa binding; ADCC and ADCP enhanced; CDC absent.

label: S298A/E333A/K334A
phenotype: Increased FcgammaRIIIa binding; ADCC enhanced.
notes: From the original alanine-scanning survey of the Fc interface.

label: margetuximab Fc
phenotype: ADCC enhanced; ADCP with FcgammaRIIa-131R absent while FcgammaRIIa-131H is retained; CDC not significantly changed.
notes: One of the few effector-enhanced Fc designs in an approved product, and the clearest case of allele-dependent behaviour across FcgammaRIIa-131H and -131R.

label: stavenhagen-set
phenotype: ADCC enhanced; CDC increased 6-fold; ADCP with FcgammaRIIa-131H increased.
notes: Reported with position 396 as P396L in the source abstract and as P396I in some catalogue renderings; IMGT lists G1v9 with V305I and P396I.

label: XmAb5574 Fc
phenotype: ADCC enhanced and ADCP with FcgammaRII increased; CDC little changed.
notes: The INN sequence carries eight substitutions while the functional literature usually describes only S239D/I332E. The six additional changes are distant from the FcgammaR interface and their contribution is not individually resolved.

label: afucosylation
therapeutics: obinutuzumab; mogamulizumab; benralizumab; inebilizumab; amivantamab; ublituximab; belantamab mafodotin
phenotype: ADCC enhanced 31-fold with FcgammaRIIIa-158V and 201-fold with FcgammaRIIIa-158F effector cells; ADCP with FcgammaRI and FcgammaRII not significantly changed.
notes: GLYCAN VARIANT, NOT A SEQUENCE VARIANT. It carries no substitutions and cannot be rendered as a mutation set, which is exactly why it belongs in the atlas: the most clinically successful ADCC enhancement to date is invisible to any tool that models Fc engineering as point mutations. Sequence-identical material differing only in core fucose spans the largest effect size in this table.

label: SELF
phenotype: Increases FcgammaRIIb binding approximately 400-fold; inhibitory ITIM signalling in B cells engaged.
notes: Selective enhancement toward the inhibitory receptor, the opposite therapeutic intent from the ADCC series while using the same interface.

label: SE
phenotype: Increased FcgammaRIIb and FcgammaRIIa-131R binding and increased C1q binding with CDC increased 3-fold; no ADCC detected with FcgammaRIIIa.

label: EFT
phenotype: Tightest reported C1q affinity in its series; CDC potency of an anti-CD20 enhanced up to 23-fold.

label: RGY
phenotype: Drives IgG hexamer formation in solution with increased C1q binding and enhanced CDC.
notes: Acts on Fc-Fc self-association rather than on the C1q contact itself, so the mechanism is assembly stoichiometry, not affinity. RGY hexamerizes in solution, which is why the single-substitution E430G is preferred therapeutically.

label: HexaBody
phenotype: Favours IgG hexamerization through increased intermolecular Fc-Fc interaction after antigen binding at the cell surface; CDC enhanced.
notes: Antigen-dependent by design: assembly is conditional on surface binding, which keeps solution-phase complement activation low.

label: Stellabody
phenotype: Hexamer-promoting substitution; increased self-association and enhanced complement potency.
notes: Self-association rank reported as wild type below E430G below E345K below E345R.

label: K326W-E333S
phenotype: Increased C1q binding and enhanced CDC.
notes: K326W alone enhances CDC while reducing ADCC, an explicit trade between arms.

label: K322A
phenotype: Reduced C1q binding and reduced CDC with FcgammaR binding largely preserved.
notes: Separates the complement arm from the cellular arm.

label: D270A
phenotype: Reduced C1q binding and reduced CDC.

label: YTE
phenotype: Approximately 10-fold increased FcRn binding at pH 6.0 with retained release at pH 7.4; 2- to 4-fold longer serum half-life in humans.
notes: The first Fc half-life engineering to be confirmed in humans. T256E contributes two new salt bridges to beta-2 microglobulin. The reference Fc-FcRn structure 4N0U carries YTE rather than wild-type Fc.

label: LS
phenotype: Approximately 11-fold higher FcRn affinity at pH 6.0; roughly 2-fold half-life increase in cynomolgus monkeys.
notes: N434S is postulated to add hydrogen bonds to FcRn.

label: QL
phenotype: Enhanced FcRn binding at pH 6.0 and extended half-life.

label: KF
phenotype: Enhanced FcRn binding at pH 6.0.

label: YTE-KFH
phenotype: Enhanced FcRn binding at pH 6.0.

label: H310A
phenotype: Abrogates FcRn binding at pH 6.0; rapid clearance.
notes: Any substitution of H310 except cysteine abolishes detectable FcRn binding. H310 is the closest Fc contact to FcRn in 4N0U at 2.04 A. Reported by IMGT on IgG2 and used across isotypes.

label: IgG3-R435H
phenotype: Extends IgG3 half-life toward that of IgG1 by restoring the IgG1 FcRn contact residue.
notes: A single residue explains most of the IgG3 half-life deficit. Histidine at 435 is the IgG1 state; arginine is the IgG3 state.

label: knob
phenotype: CH3 knob; pairs with the T366S/L368A/Y407V hole to drive heavy-chain heterodimerization.
notes: Partner variant required; see KiH-hole.

label: hole
phenotype: CH3 hole; pairs with the T366W knob to drive heavy-chain heterodimerization.
notes: Obligate partner design. Half a knobs-into-holes pair on one chain is a destabilizing mutation, not a bispecific platform.

label: original knob
phenotype: First-generation CH3 knob, paired with Y407T.

label: original hole
phenotype: First-generation CH3 hole, paired with T366Y.

label: cFAE
phenotype: With a K409R partner chain, permits controlled Fab-arm exchange to assemble bispecific IgG1 from two parental antibodies.
notes: Partner variant K409R required on the second chain.

label: cFAE partner
phenotype: Partner chain for controlled Fab-arm exchange; dissociation of the K409R parent into half-molecules is rate-controlling.

label: DD
phenotype: Charge-reversed CH3 face; pairs with the E356K/D399K chain to favour heterodimer over homodimer.
notes: Partner variant required; see charge-pair-KK.

label: KK
phenotype: Charge-reversed CH3 face; pairs with the K392D/K409D chain to favour heterodimer over homodimer.
notes: ALLOTYPE DEPENDENCE. The published substitution is written E356K, but the UniProt IGHG1 reference sequence P01857 carries aspartate at EU 356. EU 356 and EU 358 are the classical IgG1 allotype pair: D356/L358 in the G1m(f) reference used here, E356/M358 in the G1m(1) allotype on which the construct was built. The substitution is real; the wild-type residue it starts from depends on the allotype of the parent antibody. Held in `disputed_mutations` so it is not silently validated against the wrong frame.

label: DE arm
phenotype: Salt-bridge heterodimerization arm; pairs with the L351K/T366K chain.

label: KK arm
phenotype: Salt-bridge heterodimerization arm; pairs with the L351D/L368E chain.

label: THIOMAB-type site
phenotype: Engineered cysteine for site-specific drug attachment.
notes: Sits inside the FcgammaR contact patch. Conjugating here is not effector-neutral, which matters for ADC design.

label: S442C
phenotype: Engineered cysteine in CH3 for site-specific drug attachment.
notes: Distal to both the FcgammaR and FcRn interfaces.

label: E272C
phenotype: Engineered cysteine for site-specific conjugation.

label: CH2-disulfide
phenotype: Engineered CH2 disulfide that stabilizes the domain in the absence of N297 glycosylation.
notes: A direct answer to the destabilization caused by glycan-knockout silencing. Often combined with N297A, N297G or N297Q.

label: SP
phenotype: Prevents IgG4 half-molecule exchange in vitro and in vivo.
notes: The single most common IgG4 modification in approved therapeutics, and not an effector-function change at all. Included to keep the distinction between stability engineering and effector engineering visible.

label: IgG4-R409K
phenotype: Reduces IgG4 half-molecule exchange.

label: IgG2-aggregation
phenotype: Reduces acid-induced aggregation with low ADCC, low FcgammaR binding, low CDC and low C1q binding.
